basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'Vers. 12. Omnis caro, Id est omnis homo. Corruperat viam suam. Id est, depravaverat'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 12. Omnis caro, Id est omnis homo. Corruperat viam suam. Id est, depravaverat actiones suas. Et ego disperdam eos cum terra. Quare dicit cum | terra, cum terra nequaquam in diluvio disperdita sit? Dicunt doctores nequaquam tantae virtutis et fecunditatis eam fuisse post diluvium quantae ante diluvium exstiterat. Unde et hominibus post diluvium esus carnium concessus est. Ante diluvium enim pomis et oleribus vescebantur. Ergo propter amissam virtutem et gratiam disperditi sunt homines cum terra.
